full_judgment:
Md Ismailuddin Sarker J: This application for leave to appeal is by defendant No. 2, Deputy Director, District Family Planning Office, Thakurgaon (Mr Mohammad Hossain) against the judgment and order dated 26-1-1995 passed by a learned Single Judge of the High Court Division in Civil Revision 166 of 1989 (Rangpur) re-numbered as Civil Revision No. 3973 of 1991 (Dhaka) affirming the judgment and order of remand dated 20-2-89 passed by the learned District Judge. Thakurgaon in Other Appeal No. 1 of 1989 setting aside the judgment and decree dated 28-9-88 passed by the Assistant Judge, Pirganj in OC Suit No. 12 of 1988. 

 4. At the hearing of the suit the plaintiffs examined their witnesses and also filed documents in support of their case, but the petitioner could not appear on that date and prayed for shifting the date of hearing on the ground that he was busy in connection with an important official meeting but the learned Munsif rejected the prayer of the petitioner for time and allowed the plaintiff-respondents to proceed with the argument of the suit. As a result the petitioner did not get any opportunity to prove his case in the suit and the suit was decreed by the trial Court. The petitioner being aggrieved preferred an appeal before the District Judge, Thakurgaon and in the appeal he filed an application on 31-1-1989 with containing documents and circulars numbering 37 in support of his case with the prayer for admitting those documents as additional evidence. The learned District Judge after hearing both the parties sent the case on remand to the trial Court for giving a chance to the petitioner to prove his case but in course of his judgment affirmed the finding of the trial Court that the suit was maintainable before the civil Court rejecting the contention of the petitioner that the civil Court had no jurisdiction to try the suit and the jurisdiction of the civil Court was barred under the provision of section 4 of the Administrative Tribunal Act, 1980. The learned Judge of the High Court Division while discharging the Rule and upholding the order of remand of the suit by the learned District Judge held that the provision of the Administrative Tribunal Act 1980 was not applicable and the suit was tribal by the civil Court.
